bandReport.notes:
Band covers Q1-Q54 contiguously across p00-p07 (printed pages 2-A, 4-A, 6-A, 8-A, 10-A, 12-A, 14-A, 16-A — the booklet is bilingual, so printed page numbers advance by two and the render has already dropped the Hindi pages).

Per-page counts, which vary: p00 Q1-8 (8), p01 Q9-15 (7), p02 Q16-23 (8), p03 Q24-30 (7), p04 Q31-38 (8), p05 Q39-45 (7), p06 Q46-49 (4 — the data-heaviest page: Q46 has four stacked-fraction options and Q47 carries three lettered statements), p07 Q50-54 (5).

DIRECTIONS SETS: NONE. There is no 'Directions:' block and no 'Consider the following for the next N items' block anywhere in p00-p07. Every question is standalone, so no setLabel/context is used in this band. Two questions LOOK set-like and are not: Q47 carries its own lettered statements S1/S2/S3 inside its stem with its four options following immediately, and Q57 (p08, band b2's territory) opens 'Consider the following statements :' with numbered items 1. and 2. followed immediately by its own options — that is also a single self-contained question, not a shared stimulus.

SEAM CHECK: there is no page before p00 (the render starts at Q1, which is complete with its four options on p00). I opened p08 and did not transcribe it: it opens cleanly at Q55 ('What is cot 1 deg cot 23 deg ... equal to?') with its full option block, so nothing straddles the p07/p08 boundary and no Directions block starts on p07 and runs into p08. My last question, Q54, is complete on p07.

FIGURES: NONE in this band. No question in Q1-Q54 refers to a printed diagram; every geometry/measurement item is stated entirely in words. Q29 and Q51 carry printed DATA TABLES (not figures) and both are transcribed inline as GFM pipe tables with separator rows.

TABLE NOTE (Q29): the printed table is a 2-row grid whose first column holds the row labels M and N; it has no natural header row, so the M row is used as the GFM header so that each M value stays paired with the N value printed directly beneath it.

RAISED MIDDLE DOT: every occurrence in this band is a DECIMAL POINT, checked individually at zoom — 5.5% (Q30), 3.75% (Q35), 0.459459459... etc. (Q34), 18.5/17.5 years (Q45), 10.5/11.5 (Q53), and the six percentages of the Q51 pie-chart table. All transcribed as full stops per the brief. No multiplication dot and no time separator occurs in p00-p07.

OVERBAR (Q23): the stem prints '0.9-with-a-vinculum-over-the-9' against a plain '0.9'; confirmed at 4x zoom and transcribed as \(0.\overline{9}\) and \(0.9\). Transcribing both as 0.9 would have destroyed the question.

RUPEE GLYPH: the booklet prints the rupee sign in Q28, Q30, Q33, Q35, Q37, Q50. Transcribed as 'Rs.' per the corpus convention.

NO MISPRINTS FOUND. Nothing in p00-p07 required a flags entry for a printed defect, and nothing was illegible.

NEIGHBOUR'S TERRITORY — b2 CHECKED AND NOW COMPLETE (no action needed): at 23:10 the file 2018-1.b2.json held only 42 questions, Q55-Q96, while its own bandReport already claimed pages [8..14] with lastComplete: true. I opened p14 (b2's last page, printed 30-A) WITHOUT transcribing it and confirmed it carries four further questions, Q97-Q100, all figure-bearing (Q97 three parallel lines cut by two transversals; Q98 an equilateral triangle with a shaded trapezium; Q99 a circle with a tangent SPT; Q100 a circle with two equal chords crossing). That is exactly the shape of the defect the brief warns about, so it was worth checking rather than assuming. It was work in progress, not a stranded tail: re-checked at 23:14, b2 holds Q55-Q100 (46 questions) and the paper is fully covered — b1 Q1-Q54 plus b2 Q55-Q100 = 100 with no gaps and no overlap. Recorded here so a later reader knows the seam WAS verified against the page rather than inferred from a clean check-bands run.

INVENTED SUBTOPIC (1): Q36 ('For 0 < m < 1, which one of the following is correct?', ordering log_10 m, m, m^2, m^-1) is filed under Logarithms with the invented subtopic 'Comparison of Logarithmic and Power Expressions' and a flags entry. The catalog's Logarithms chapter lists only identities/change-of-base, solving log equations, and digits-and-characteristic; the Inequalities chapter lists only linear, modulus and quadratic. Neither covers ordering a log against powers, so per the brief the closest chapter is used and the gap is reported rather than forced.
